issues.description: The problem statement and the example Main refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon, but the solution implements a static method with a different name (receiveDelivery(String, int, int)). This name mismatch (acceptSupplyDelivery vs. receiveDelivery) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which method to implement and will cause example usage or tests expecting acceptSupplyDelivery to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across all artifacts. Either rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...), or update the problem statement and example Main to refer to receiveDelivery(...). Ensure the signature remains (String name, int price, int quantity) and the method is static on SealSaloon.

issues.description: The problem statement and template reference a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(...) to add delivered ingredients to the shared stock, but the solution implements this operation as a static method named receiveDelivery(...). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery / updating stock quantities) can confuse students: the example call in Main uses acceptSupplyDelivery, while the solution's SealSaloon provides receiveDelivery, making it unclear which method name to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the delivery-accepting method across all artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (and update any internal references), or update the problem statement and template Main to call receiveDelivery(...). Ensure the method signature remains static and matches the documented parameters (String name, int price, int quantity).
